title: Microsoft Edge: expanded enforcement controls for Data Loss Prevention connectors
notes: claim 65: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing says administrator guidance is not documented, but Microsoft now documents the custom_messages policy field for paste, upload and print. The justification row also incorrectly says no UI is documented even though its policy can be configured in Group Policy Editor. The roadmap status and January 2027 target remain accurate.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and api; controls[3].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No setting, UI or automation is documented for administrator-defined guidance shown to users.
claims.quote: custom_messages Provides administrator guidance for non-clean analysis results. Each entry identifies a tag and a message. GP unique name: OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector. Value name: OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector
claims.fix: Set controls[3].api.kind to 'other', call to 'custom_messages field in OnBulkDataEntryEnterpriseConnector policy (Group Policy or registry)', and docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies/onbulkdataentryenterpriseconnector. Set its UI to Group Policy Editor, path 'Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Configuration policy for bulk data entry for Microsoft Edge for Business Data Loss Prevention Connectors', with the same docs. Replace the note with 'The paste policy custom_messages field supplies tag-based guidance for non-clean results. Each entry identifies a tag and a message; new messages must be non-empty and at most 200 displayed characters. Verdict-provided messages take precedence.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/configure-microsoft-edge for the entry route. Replace the matching prose absence with this documented field, and narrow the open question to whether the Edge Management Service exposes custom_messages.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure and Autonomy; Scope
claims.claim: Enabled DLP connectors send content from specific user actions to an on-device agent.
claims.quote: When enabled, Microsoft Edge sends content from specific user actions to the on-device agent

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters
claims.claim: Edge for Business natively enforces the on-device DLP agent's verdicts.
claims.quote: Microsoft Edge for Business Data Loss Prevention Connectors enable Microsoft Edge for Business to natively enforce DLP (Data Loss Prevention) verdicts from on-device agents.

claims.claim: Setting block_until_verdict to 1 makes Edge wait for the analysis response before allowing page access to the data.
claims.quote: block_until_verdict If set to 1, Microsoft Edge waits for a response from the analysis service before giving the page access to the data.

claims.claim: Any other integer block_until_verdict value allows immediate page access.
claims.quote: Any other integer value allows the page to access the data immediately.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The fallback verdict setting determines what happens when communication between Edge and the DLP agent fails.
claims.quote: Choose to 'Allow file access' or 'Block file access'. This determines the default verdict if a communication error between Edge and the DLP agent occurs.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Setting default_action to block denies page access if contacting the analysis service fails.
claims.quote: default_action If set to block, Microsoft Edge denies page access to the data if an error occurs while contacting the analysis service.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A default_action value other than block permits page access on a communication failure.
claims.quote: Any other value permits the page to access the data.

claims.claim: Symantec recommends allow as the default_action value, so that configuration allows content through on communication failure.
claims.quote: Configure the following fields in the policy with the recommended values from Symantec: default_action | allow
